newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: New Zambian cabinet warned on corruption.
newsitem.headline: New Zambian cabinet warned on corruption.

text.p: Zambia's new cabinet was sworn in on Tuesday with President Frederick Chiluba warning that he would not condone corruption in his government.

"It is important that you are not involved in shoddy dealings. Do not look to me to save you from whatever trouble you get in because of your misdeeds," said Chiluba, whose first cabinet was persistenly accused of corruption.
"I do not want to suffer because of your inefficiency or mistakes. Before I get chopped, I will chop you instead," he said.
Chiluba named a new cabinet on Monday in which most of his former advisers, including his vice-president Godfrey Miyanda, retained their positions.
Other aides who kept their old positions were minister without portfolio Michael Sata, defence minister Ben Mwila, home affairs minister Chitalu Sampa and finance minister Ronald Penza.
Chiluba's ruling Movement for Multi-party Democracy (MMD) scored a landslide victory at controversial elections that were boycotted by seven opposition parties last month.

Former president Kenneth Kaunda's United National Independence Party (UNIP), which led the opposition boycott, warned on Monday that it would press ahead with a civil disobedience campaign against Chiluba's government.
Chiluba, who suffered resignations in his last cabinet over differences on constitutional reform, told his new ministers at Tuesday's swearing-in ceremony that he expected complete loyalty from them.
"Collective responsibility is extremely important in this government. There must never be any divisions among us when we go to Parliament," he said.
